meta.title: CPO Prep — Practice Quiz
meta.disclaimer: This is prep material only. Official CPO certification requires enrollment with an authorized provider (PHTA / NSPF).
meta.authoring: 100% original, in-house authorship. Questions do not reproduce content from any commercial CPO course.

questions.prompt: Which pH range provides the best balance between bather comfort and chlorine effectiveness?
questions.explanation: Codes and best practice place pool pH in the 7.2–7.8 band; chlorine loses most of its killing power above pH 8.

questions.prompt: Total alkalinity primarily functions as a:
questions.explanation: Total alkalinity buffers the water against pH swings when acids or bases are added.

questions.prompt: Low calcium hardness (below ~200 ppm) is most likely to cause:

choices.text: Corrosion of plaster and metal surfaces

questions.explanation: Under-saturated water becomes aggressive and leaches calcium out of plaster, grout, and heat exchangers.

questions.prompt: Cyanuric acid (CYA) is used to:

choices.text: Protect free chlorine from UV degradation

questions.explanation: CYA absorbs UV energy that would otherwise destroy chlorine within hours.

questions.prompt: Combined chlorine (CC) should be kept below approximately:
questions.explanation: CC above 0.2 ppm indicates irritant chloramine build-up and warrants breakpoint action.

questions.prompt: A slightly POSITIVE Langelier Saturation Index (LSI) indicates the water tends to:
questions.explanation: Positive LSI indicates supersaturation; scale deposition is expected above roughly +0.5.

questions.prompt: At pH 7.5, roughly what fraction of free chlorine exists as the strongly-disinfecting hypochlorous acid (HOCl)?
questions.explanation: At pH ~7.5 the HOCl/OCl- ratio is close to 50/50; sanitizing power drops sharply as pH climbs.

questions.prompt: Which chlorine product raises cyanuric acid the fastest per ppm of chlorine added?
questions.explanation: Trichlor is a stabilized chlorine; every 10 ppm FAC added by trichlor also adds ~6 ppm CYA.

questions.prompt: Reaching 'breakpoint' chlorination generally requires raising free chlorine to approximately:
questions.explanation: Rule of thumb: FAC ≈ 10 × CC destroys chloramines chemically and returns the residual to free form.

questions.prompt: A salt-chlorine generator produces its sanitizer by:

choices.text: Electrolyzing dissolved salt into hypochlorous acid

questions.explanation: SCG electrolyzes NaCl at ~3000-3500 ppm across a titanium cell to generate chlorine on-site.

questions.prompt: The characteristic sharp 'pool smell' at an indoor pool is caused primarily by:
questions.explanation: Trichloramine and dichloramine are volatile irritants; the smell means CC is too high, not that chlorine is.

questions.prompt: When CYA has risen above ~100 ppm and combined chlorine will not clear, the correct field response is to:

choices.text: Partial drain and refill to dilute CYA

questions.explanation: You cannot chemically remove CYA in-service; dilution is the only field-practical fix.

questions.prompt: The purpose of a pool filter is to:

choices.text: Remove suspended solids so sanitizer can work

questions.explanation: Filters clarify — they do not disinfect. Sanitizer does the disinfection.

questions.prompt: A typical residential pool turnover target is:
questions.explanation: Residential filtration systems are sized so the entire pool volume passes the filter every 8–12 hours.

questions.prompt: Which filter media provides the finest particle capture in normal use?
questions.explanation: DE captures down to ~3–5 microns; sand captures 20–40 microns, cartridge ~10–15.

questions.prompt: Backwashing is required when the filter pressure gauge rises above the clean baseline by approximately:
questions.explanation: 8–10 psi rise indicates the filter is fully loaded and flow is being restricted.

questions.prompt: Cartridge filters are cleaned by:

choices.text: Hose-rinsing the pleats and periodic detergent soak

questions.explanation: Cartridges are never backwashed; they are pulled and cleaned manually.

questions.prompt: Total Dynamic Head (TDH) describes:

choices.text: The vertical height of the pool wall
The total resistance the pump must overcome
The chlorine demand of the pool

questions.explanation: TDH is the sum of all suction, friction, and elevation resistances the pump moves water against.

questions.prompt: Which side of the pump is most vulnerable to air leaks that destroy prime and can damage the seal?
questions.explanation: Suction-side leaks pull air in and cause cavitation; return-side leaks lose water but do not un-prime the pump.

questions.prompt: The Virginia Graeme Baker (VGB) Act requires public pools to use suction fittings certified under:
questions.explanation: ANSI/APSP/ICC-16 is the suction-fitting standard referenced by the VGB Act.

questions.prompt: A variable-speed pump running at half speed uses approximately what fraction of the energy per hour of full-speed operation?
questions.explanation: Pump power scales roughly with the cube of speed; half speed ≈ 1/8 power draw.

questions.prompt: Cavitation inside the pump most commonly sounds like:

choices.text: Marbles rattling in the pump housing

questions.explanation: Vapor bubbles collapse violently, producing the characteristic marbles-in-a-can sound and destroying impellers.

questions.prompt: The primary reason chlorine cannot rapidly kill Cryptosporidium is:

choices.text: It has a chlorine-resistant oocyst wall
It only grows at high pH

questions.explanation: The Cryptosporidium oocyst wall gives it extreme chlorine resistance; even 20 ppm FAC takes 10+ hours.

questions.prompt: The CDC MAHC diarrheal-accident hyperchlorination protocol requires FAC of approximately:
questions.explanation: MAHC recommends FAC 20 ppm at pH ≤ 7.5 for 12.75 hours after a diarrheal fecal event.

questions.prompt: UV disinfection installed in the return line is best described as:

choices.text: A supplemental treatment that still requires a chlorine residual

questions.explanation: UV kills a wide range of pathogens on pass, but leaves no residual; chlorine is still required in the pool.

questions.prompt: Spa waters at 100–104 °F create an environment friendly to:
questions.explanation: Legionella thrives in warm, biofilm-rich water; spa sanitation targets are stricter than pool targets.

questions.prompt: The single most effective operational practice for reducing recreational water illness at a public pool is:
questions.explanation: Pre-swim showers remove ~90% of the organics bathers bring into the pool, cutting chloramine and demand.

questions.prompt: During a formed-stool fecal accident (per MAHC), the required FAC is approximately:
questions.explanation: Formed-stool response: raise to FAC 2 ppm at pH ≤ 7.5, hold 25 min. Diarrheal events are stricter.

questions.prompt: An erosion (tablet) feeder works by:

choices.text: Injecting liquid via a diaphragm pump
Diverting a small stream of return water through a tablet chamber

questions.explanation: The regulated flow through the tablet chamber controls the dissolution rate and thus the chlorine feed.

questions.prompt: A peristaltic metering pump delivers liquid chemical by:

choices.text: Rotating a roller to squeeze a flexible tube

questions.explanation: A rotating roller collapses the tube, moving a precisely-defined volume per revolution.

questions.prompt: A salt cell should typically be cleaned with dilute muriatic acid:

choices.text: Every 3–6 months, only if calcium buildup is present

questions.explanation: Over-cleaning erodes the catalytic coating and shortens cell life; clean only when needed.

questions.prompt: ORP measures the water's:
questions.explanation: ORP is a proxy for disinfection potential; a controller compares to a setpoint and doses accordingly.

questions.prompt: A liquid-chemical feed system must always be interlocked with the:

choices.text: Circulation pump (and ideally a flow switch)

questions.explanation: Dosing without flow can concentrate chemical in the pipe and damage equipment or create a hazard.

questions.prompt: A Safety Data Sheet (SDS) must be:

choices.text: Locked in the office manager's desk
Readily accessible to anyone who may handle the chemical

questions.explanation: OSHA Hazard Communication requires SDSs be readily accessible during every work shift.

questions.prompt: The correct order when diluting muriatic acid is:

choices.text: They can be added in either order

questions.explanation: Always add acid to a large volume of water; the reverse can violently boil and splash acid.

questions.prompt: Which pair of chemicals must NEVER be stored in the same container or near each other?
questions.explanation: Trichlor + cal-hypo can react exothermically and ignite; keep separated with clean scoops for each.

questions.prompt: Baseline PPE for routine chemical handling should include at minimum:

choices.text: Chemical-splash goggles AND gloves AND closed-toe shoes AND long pants

questions.explanation: OSHA HCS and typical SDS Section 8 require eye, hand, foot, and skin protection at a minimum.

questions.prompt: An eyewash station must be capable of providing continuous flushing for at least:
questions.explanation: ANSI Z358.1 sets the 15-minute continuous-flow standard for emergency eyewash.

questions.prompt: Before servicing electrical pool equipment, the operator must:

choices.text: Cut power at the disconnect and verify dead with a meter
Wait for the sun to set

questions.explanation: Lockout-tagout and verification with a meter is required; never rely on a switch alone.

questions.prompt: The Virginia Graeme Baker Act is enforced primarily by the:
questions.explanation: CPSC has enforcement authority for consumer product safety, including VGB drain-cover compliance.

questions.prompt: The ANSI/APSP/ICC-11 standard covers:
questions.explanation: APSP-11 is the industry water-quality standard; states adopt it as the floor for FAC/pH/TA/CH ranges.

questions.prompt: The CDC's Model Aquatic Health Code (MAHC) is:

choices.text: A voluntary, evidence-based model code that states may adopt

questions.explanation: MAHC is voluntary; jurisdictions adopt in whole, part, or reference — many use it as best-practice benchmark.

questions.prompt: Under the ADA 2010 Standards, most public pools must provide accessible entry via:

choices.text: A pool lift, sloped entry, transfer wall, or transfer system

questions.explanation: The ADA 2010 Standards enumerate multiple compliant accessible-entry options for public pools.

questions.prompt: A typical residential-code minimum pool barrier height is at least:
questions.explanation: The ISPSC typically requires at least a 48-inch barrier (60 inches in some jurisdictions).

questions.prompt: A rectangular pool 30 ft × 15 ft with an average depth of 5 ft holds approximately:
To raise free chlorine by 1 ppm in 10,000 gallons using cal-hypo (73%), you need approximately:
questions.explanation: ~1.9 oz cal-hypo (73%) per 10,000 gal per ppm FAC is the standard field factor.

questions.prompt: One U.S. gallon of water weighs approximately:
questions.explanation: One U.S. gallon of water ≈ 8.33 lb (7.48 gal = 1 cu ft, not lb/gal).

questions.prompt: 10 ppm alkalinity in 10,000 gal is raised by approximately how much sodium bicarbonate?
questions.explanation: ~1.5 lb of sodium bicarbonate per 10,000 gal raises TA by ~10 ppm.

questions.prompt: In what order should routine chemistry adjustments generally be made?
questions.explanation: TA first (it drives pH), then pH, then CYA if needed, then FAC last — otherwise chlorine is wasted at high pH.

questions.prompt: If a pool's FAC is 1.5 ppm and CC is 0.8 ppm, the breakpoint target FAC is approximately:
questions.explanation: Breakpoint ≈ 10 × CC = 10 × 0.8 = 8.0 ppm FAC to burn out chloramines.
